intent: Generalise the fresh-install/main.sh split method into a reusable script, so the remaining shell splits do not repeat the line-range mistake that broke the first attempt.
scope: Non-goal: any split; this commit only adds the tool
changes: extract_shell_functions.py walks the script brace-by-brace, lifts only top-level function blocks (with the comment directly above each), and leaves every other line in place - so interleaved top-level commands cannot be swept into the library.

It inserts the source directive after the `set -e`/`set -euo pipefail` line, with a `# shellcheck source=` comment relative to the script's own directory, matching the repo convention for new sourced libs.
--functions moves a named subset, for scripts where only part of the body should leave.
It exits non-zero if a named function does not exist, or if there is no `set -e` line to anchor the source directive, rather than producing a subtly wrong file.

verification.command: Re-derive the already-verified fresh-install/main.sh split in a throwaway worktree at HEAD~1, then diff against the committed result
verification.evidence: main.sh: IDENTICAL. lib/packages.sh: IDENTICAL. The tool reproduces byte-for-byte a split that was verified by hand with the shfmt harness, a structural flow comparison, and a source-time side-effect check.
Prints usage for script, library, --functions and --header.
All hooks pass. A T201 print warning was fixed by writing to sys.stdout rather than suppressed.

risks: The brace counter treats { and } inside strings and heredocs as structural. A function containing an unbalanced brace in a string would be mis-delimited; verify_shell_split.sh reports the function count, so this shows up as a wrong count rather than silently.
It assumes the `name() {` form on one line. A script using `function name {` or a brace on the next line would have those functions ignored - again visible as a lower count in the verifier.
rollback: git revert the commit; the tool disappears and the already-committed splits are unaffected, since it only generates files.
No follow-up validation needed after rollback.
